newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Farmers hamstrung by rain.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Farmers hamstrung by rain.

text.p: Farmers' attempts at harvesting fall crops and planting hard red winter wheat continued to be hampered by rains, and grain merchandisers said more showers were due Friday in the High Plains states.
"It's been very, very wet. We had some localized flooding yesterday in the eastern two-thirds of Oklahoma," one northern Oklahoma dealer said.
"It looks like they're already getting more rain down in the Oklahoma Panhandle and northern Texas, which means it's probably coming straight for us," a central Kansas dealer said.

Dealers said some farmers were getting a little nervous about not being able to harvest their sorghum crop. But they said producers were taking comfort in the National Weather Service's six- to 10-day outlook, which called for a return to dry weather next week.
Basis bids remained mostly steady and movement was slow, dealers said.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
